_about: How the Takemikazuchi mesh is hung on the stock Ronin skeleton.  Hand-authored; this file is the retarget.
The skin keeps every Ronin bone.  Each Takemikazuchi joint's vertices are placed onto, and weighted to, Ronin bones.
{S} is L or R (Takemikazuchi side suffix), {s} is l or r (Ronin side infix).
block:    joints that stay one rigid piece with the torso (uniform scale, no rotation), and the Ronin bone they follow.
segments: a straight Takemikazuchi limb section (from joint -> to joint) laid along a chain of Ronin bones.
stretch = axial   : lengthened or shortened along its axis so both ends meet Ronin's joints
uniform : scaled evenly (up to max_scale) so the far end approaches Ronin's joint
none    : plain scale, far end left where it falls
align = false     : keep the section's own orientation instead of turning it onto the Ronin bone
joints            : which Takemikazuchi joints ride this section; a bone name pins their vertices to that
bone, null weights them by where they fall along the Ronin chain
_legs: Ronin's leg has three bones in a zig-zag (thigh, thighLow, knee); the Takemikazuchi's is a straight thigh and shin.
The legs are NOT folded along Ronin's bones.  They stay exactly as the Takemikazuchi has them - straight, under its
own hips, part of the rigid block - and are only weighted to Ronin's leg bones by height (see 'banded').  Standing,
the leg is straight; when Ronin's leg folds, it flexes softly around the two heights where Ronin's joints are.

_about: The user's rule (2026-11-15): 'Just use the Project MIKHAIL model how it is but scale it up so it's the same size as
the Ronin.'  So the body is ONE rigid, evenly scaled copy of the model - head, chest, shoulder armour, hips, legs,
feet, jump units and mounts keep their sculpted places - and the scale is not a hand-picked number: it is Ronin's
overall height divided by the Takemikazuchi's (antenna included), about 11.54 units per metre.
Only the arms, from the shoulder joint down, leave the rigid body: they are laid along Ronin's arm bones, because
they have to swing at Ronin's joints and the hands have to reach Ronin's weapons.
History: 11.09 (shoulders on Ronin's joints) read as too small; 12% bigger with the arms and shoulder armour left
behind at Ronin's joint height was rejected at once ('Why did you move the chest up', 'It looks fat now').  Do not
move or resize parts of the body relative to each other.

anchor._about: lined up front-to-back and side-to-side at the shoulders; vertically the soles stand on Ronin's ground

_about: Parts that must end up where a plain scaled copy of the model has them, relative to each other.  The build stops if the
centre of any of them is further than max_shift_units from that place.  (Only the arms from the shoulder joint down
are re-posed, onto Ronin's arm bones; everything else is listed here.)
Pieces of the model that are not put on the body, at the owner's request (2026-11-15: 'can you remove those small
blades in the hand? They look off').  Knife_L / Knife_R each carry one separate piece and nothing else: the
forearm blade, 3.6 m long and 8 cm thin, which the model has run out past the fingertips.  Every triangle that
follows a listed joint is dropped; the forearm it slides out of is a different piece and is untouched.
The upper-arm joint also carries the shoulder fittings that sit tucked under the shoulder armour (the pod with
the fin, its mounting bar and bolts, the link to the collar).  They are separate pieces of mesh that end well
above the elbow.  Any connected piece on this joint that ends before this fraction of the way from shoulder to
elbow stays where the model has it, as part of the rigid body, and follows the same bone as the shoulder armour;
only the arm itself goes onto Ronin's arm bones.  Without this the pod hangs 9 units low and a gap opens under
the armour (found by review, 2026-11-15).

banded.name: leg
banded._about: placed with the rigid block; weighted by height to these bones, changing over at the heights of the named Ronin joints

bodygroups._about: Ronin hides or swaps these groups for damage states; each bone's vertices go to its group
